newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOCUS-Denmark opens mobile phone market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Denmark opens mobile phone market.

text.p: Denmark took a further step towards opening up its telecoms industry on Wednesday, licensing two new operators to offer mobile phone services alongside existing providers Tele Danmark and Sonofon.

The regulatory National Telecom Agency said in a statement that it had granted licences to the two Danish operators and to Sweden's Telia and to France Telecom to operate DCS 1800 systems, a multi-operator refinement of existing GSM technology.
"With this tender round, the foundations are prepared for Danish mobile telephone operators to be offered in future services at prices which have never here been lower," it said.

"The appointment of new operators in the mobile telephone sector should be seen as a move toward the political goal of ensuring real and free competition in the telecoms industry so that consumers get wider choice and better and cheaper service."
Telia, it said, had also been licensed to operate the ERMES European paging system in Denmark.
The Swedish state-owned operator said that it planned to invest over one billion crowns on its DCS 1800 network, including erecting 700-800 masts.
France Telecom said its budget for the system was 1.1 billion crowns over 10 years and its Danish unit Mobilix planned to double the total number of mobile phone subscribers.

"Denmark, with its 5.2 million residents, has one of the most developed telecommunications networks in Europe. Tele Danmark and Sonofon share about 1.5 million mobile phone subscribers, which is equal to about 26 percent of the population," it added.
"It is Mobilix's goal to increase the number of subscribers to at least 55 percent over a 10-year period by introducing new telephony services and a price policy that is simple and clear."
Tele Danmark, which already has a head-start said it would spend 600 million by the year 2000 and aimed at 50 percent geographical coverage.

In addition to allowing several operators in the same market the new system also offers dual-use of mobile telephones, allowing them to be used at home through the fixed-line network at around fixed-line prices.
Sonofon, which sought and received a license for a lower-powered system than the other three licensees, said it would use it to supplement its existing national GSM network in high-traffic areas.
It said that the need for further investment would therefore be limited.
In its 1996 annual report on Tuesday Tele Danmark said that deregulation, begun last July and expected to be completed shortly, would inevitably mean lost market share.
"The liberalisation of July 1 1996 means growing competition which will result in the further loss of (our) market share in the area of telephony," it said.
"We therefore expect telephone charges to come under pressure with prices falling overall as a result," it added.

The company is particularly irked by pending government price-capping of access to Tele Danmark's network by competitors which it says compels unreasonably low charges. --Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
